 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.09.2020.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 15.09.2020 at about 5.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his bike bearing No. KA-02-HU-4249 towards Rajajinagar to Yeshwanathpura K.N. extension road,
along with his customer at that time the rider of another bike bearing No.
KA-04-JW-8295 came from cross road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's bike.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Loan Officer at Ujjivan Small Finance and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner, insured and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 remained absent hence, placed exparte.

Respondent No.3 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement admitting the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the accident was happened due to negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
Also contended that the rider of the offending motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.3 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW- 8295 by its rider, in RTA took place on 15.09.2020 at about 5.30 p.m. near K N Extension, Triveni Road,
Yeshvanthapura, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P14 to 20.
Respondent No.3 examined its official as RW.1. and got marked Ex.R1.

Also examined ASI, Yeshwanthapura Traffic PS as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R2 & 3.
6.
Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of-examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, first information statement, spot mahazar along with sketch, notice issued to owner of the vehicle and reply, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner himself in the hospital.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and sketch was conducted.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and the rough sketch therein, the alleged accident place is in the middle of the circle where the four roads were joining.
But if we perused the contents of mahazar along with rough sketch, the main cause for the alleged accident is changing of lane by the rider of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295.
Thus, it shows that the negligence is on the part of the rider of the bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295.
No doubt that as per Ex.P5 no damages were found at the time of inspection on vehicle bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295.

sentences.text: But this alone will not sufficient to hold that the said vehicle is not involved in the accident.

10. If we perused the Ex.P2 statement given by the petitioner in an hospital, the petitioner has given his statement in hospital on 15.9.2020 at about 8.45 p.m. by alleging the accident on the very same day at 5.30 p.m.
Thus, the statement of the victim and FIR is registered within four hours of accident thus, it can be construed that the vehicle bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 is involved in the accident.

Further Ex.P6 wound certificate also speaks that the petitioner admitted to the hospital with the history of road traffic accident near Yeshwanthpur circle at 5.30 p.m. on 15.9.2020.
11.
As discussed above, as per mahazar the accident is in the middle of the road and caused by the negligence of the rider of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW- 8295.
As per Ex.P7 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the rider of the offending bike wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-829.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the bike bearing No.
KA-04-JW-8295.
13.
The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence riding.
The respondent no.3
even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The respondent No.1 to 3 even after sufficient opportunity have not lead any evidence to disprove the contents of these documents.

The charge sheet is came to be filed on the rider of the offending vehicle KA-04-JW-8295 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC and Sec. 134(A) (b), R/w. Sec. 187, 3 (1), R/w. Sec.181 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024

16. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.3 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence with some unknown vehicle, the same is not established and nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
17. The contents of Ex.P4 spot mahazar falsifies the contention of respondent no.3 about the contributory negligence of petitioner for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 7 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P 7 charge sheet also supports the view of this court, as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC and Sec. 134(A) (b), R/w. Sec. 187, 3 (1),
R/w. Sec.181 of IMV Act against the driver of the bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295.
18.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 15.09.2020 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. No.KA-04-JW- 8295 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 32 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P8 also shows that the petitioner was aged about 32 years at the time of accident.
In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to columbia Asia Hospital.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner admitted to Columbia Asia Hospital on 17.9.2020 and discharged on 20.9.2020.

As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the petitioner Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172208460/

b) Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11, amounting to Rs.2,02,481/-.
But at the time of cross-examination he has admitted that Rs.1,20,000/- is paid by the health insurance company.
If we perused the inpatient bill marked at Ex.P11 out of total expenditure of Rs.1,81,809/-, Rs.1,60,809/- is paid by the health insurance company and remaining Rs.40,802/- is paid by the petitioner.
Apart from this bill, the other bills marked at SL. No.17 & 18 are advance deposit receipt hence, they cannot be reimbursed.
The bill marked at SL.No.19 is liable to be reimbursed hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.40,802/- + Rs.700/-= Rs.41,502/- by rounding of the same to Rs.42,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as Loan officer at Ujjivan Small Finance Ltd., and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2020.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P10- the petitioner was admitted to Columbia Asia Hospital on 17.09.2020 and discharged on 20.9.2020 for 4 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in two month period including 4 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 2 months = Rs.29,000/-
during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.
Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital as PW.3, through him outpatient record and X-ray film are marked at Ex.P.19 & 20.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained displaced oblique fracture of the shaft of left tibia with healed fibula fracture.
He underwent surgery in the form of closed reduction and internal fixation left tibia with IMIL nailing under SA on 18.9.2020.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered total disability of both limbs at 36% and whole body disability at 18%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
Further PW.2 has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may costs Rs.25,000/-.

According to the petitioner he was working as field Executive at Ujjivan Small Finance Co. Ltd.,
Admittedly, the petitioner has not produced any salary certificate or any resignation letter to show that he has left the said job due to the disability caused to him.
But neither the resignation letter nor the account statement to s how that he is not receiving the salary is not produced by the petitioner.
The petitioner sustained major fractures of tibia and fibula of the left leg.
Even though it is operated and corrected by the surgery, certainly the functional disability is going to be caused due to the said fracture or implants.
To establish the disability the petitioner examined the doctor wherein he assessed 18% whole body disability.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, this Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172208460/
6 court is of the opinion that the injuries sustained by the petitioner will certainly effect on his work and day-today life.

The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card marked at Ex.P8, as per this document the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1988.
The accident was occurred in the year-2020.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 32 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '16'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,500/- X 12 X 16 X 12% =Rs.3,34,080/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.P8 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 4 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 4 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.4,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.15,000/- under this head.

 20. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 to 3 are the owner, insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.3 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the motor cycle bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 and the policy was in force at the time of accident.

21. Now that this court has ascertained the compensation amount, the last aspect of the matter is regarding fixation of liability i.e., who should be made liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner?

Precisely, it is the specific case of the respondent No.3 that the respondent No.1 has handed over the offending vehicle bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 to a person who has not having valid driving license.

To establish the said fact, the respondent No.3 initially relied on Ex.P7 charge sheet wherein Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC and Sec. 134(A) (b), R/w. Sec. 187, 3 (1), R/w. Sec.181 of IMV Act are invoked against the rider of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295.

On perusal of the Ex.P7 at the time of accident one Yarab was the driver of the said bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 and it is found that he was not having valid licence at the time of accident to ride the said vehicle.

The Ex.P4 the notice and reply under Sec.133 of IMV Act wherein the respondent No.1 has given statement that the rider of bike bearing No. KA-04- JW-8295 was not having valid licence at the time of accident to ride the said bike.
The respondent No.1 even though served with notice has not made any denial to the said documents.
The petitioner has not made out any contradictory evidence in respect of the contents of these police documents.
22. The respondent No.3 insurance company also summoned the Investigation Officer and examined as RW.2.

The RW.2 also deposed that the rider of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 was Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172208460/

23. For the reasons discussed as supra, it is established that the rider of the offending vehicle bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 was not having valid licence at the time of the accident.
24. The next aspect to be pondered upon now is, what is the effect of the rider of the offending vehicle not possessing a driving license at the time of accident.

In H.K. Shivaramu Vs.
H.S.Shivaramum other rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on 4.12.2020 wherein in a similar set of facts the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held thus:
10. On the basis of the evidence of the parties and the materials available on record,
i.e., Ex.P2 - charge sheet the Tribunal has rightly held that the rider of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence and fastened the liability on the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 - the rider and the owner of the offending vehicle jointly and severally.

entities.text: Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In view of the law laid down by a Full Bench of this Court in the case of YELLAVVA (supra), even though there is violation of policy conditions, when it is not in dispute that as on the date of the accident the offending vehicle was covered by the insurance policy, the insurance company has to pay the compensation with liberty to recover the same.

25. The essence of the said decision is that even where the driver of the offending vehicle was found to be driving without a valid driving license and the insurance company pleads that there is violation of policy conditions, if the vehicle had a valid and subsisting insurance policy, then the insurance company has to pay the compensation with liberty to recover the same from owner and rider.

26. In fact the Hon'ble Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka relied upon the decision of Hon'ble full bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in New India Assurance Co.,
Ltd., vs Yallavva reported in ILR 2020 Kar 2239 equivalent (2020) 2 KCCR 1405 wherein the Hon'ble High court has reaffirmed the principles relating to pay and recover by relying upon decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh and Others reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297 cited supra held thus:
34.

sentences.text: On a reading of the same, it becomes clear that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down two tests.

The breach of a policy condition, for example, by disqualification of the driver to hold a driving licence or invalid driving licence has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

In other words, in order to avoid the liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of policy regarding use of the vehicle by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

Thus,
Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172208460/
9 burden of proof of establishing breach on the part of the owner of the vehicle is on the Insurance Company.

entities.text: Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above is the first test laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Then, there is another test enunciated.

Even after proving breach of a policy condition regarding a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period on the part of the insured, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid his liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches is/are so "fundamental" as found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

This is having regard to the "rule of main purpose" or "main purpose rule" i.e., even if there is a proof of the driver of a motor vehicle not being duly licenced at the time of the accident, the said fact must be a cause for the accident.
In other words, the breach was so fundamental as to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The doctrine of fundamental breach has been incorporated in Section 149 of the Act by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in order to give effect to the main purpose rule.
Thus, the exclusion clause or the defence of an insurer so as to avoid liability has been read down to the extent to which it is inconsistent to the main purpose of the contract.
The above is the second test to be applied.

Thus,
there has to be a finding of fact, as to, whether, the owner or the insured had taken reasonable care.
Hence, the Tribunal will have to decide the dispute, as to, whether, the insurer has proved its defence.

While adjudicating the said claim if the Tribunal concludes that the insurer has satisfactorily proved its defence in accordance with Section 149(2)(a) of the Act, the Tribunal can direct that the insurer is liable to be reimbursed by the insured for the compensation and other amounts which it has been compelled to pay to the third party as per the award of the Tribunal having regard to the mandate of section 149(1) of the Act."

(emphasis supplied by me) The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh and Others reported in (2004) 3 SCC 297 cited supra has categorically held that to avoid its liability towards insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further at para 110 the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed thus:
(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g., disqualification of driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of section 149, have to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.
Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards insured,
the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

(emphasis supplied by me)

sentences.text: No doubt the respondent No.3 insurance company has proved that the rider of bike bearing No.KA-04-JW-8295 did not possess license, but the above decision makes it clear that the respondent No.3 was required to prove that the insured was negligent or did not exercise reasonable care which is not proved.

Thereby fortifying the view taken by this court that the respondent No.3 should make good the compensation amount to the petitioner and then proceed against the respondent No.1 i.e., the owner to recover the same.

sentences.text: In the case reported in (2018) 9 SCC 650, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has summarised the concept of pay and recovery wherein it has held that in case of breach of policy condition the pay and recover can be ordered in case of third party risks.

Further, in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 9827-2012 has held that when there is no allegation that when the owner was not negligent not verified the driving licence of rider, under such circumstances the principle of pay and recovery can be made applicable.
29. In this case, the respondent No.1 & 2 are placed exparte.

The respondent No.3 has not issued any notice or taken any steps to show that the owner of bike bearing No. KA-04-JW-8295 has intentionally and with the knowledge handed over the bike to the person who was not having valid licence.
No evidence is available to hold that the owner intentionally and with the knowledge has violated the conditions of the policy.

For the foregoing reasons this court finds no hesitation in holding that the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.3 being the insurer shall pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with liberty to recover the same from respondent No.1 & 2.

Accordingly, Issue No. II is held in the partly affirmative and it is held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,09,080/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum and it is also held that the respondent No.3 shall pay the compensation amount as awarded by this court to the petitioner and recover the same from respondent No.1 & 2 and this issue is answered accordingly.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 Girish Kakde A.S vs Mohammed Shokath on 13 June, 2024

Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 15.09.2020 which is caused by the rider of the motor cycle bearing No. No.KA-04-JW- 8295 which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.

25. The essence of the said decision is that even where the driver of the offending vehicle was found to be driving without a valid driving license and the insurance company pleads that there is violation of policy conditions, if the vehicle had a valid and subsisting insurance policy, then the insurance company has to pay the compensation with liberty to recover the same from owner and rider.
In other words, in order to avoid the liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of policy regarding use of the vehicle by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.
Even after proving breach of a policy condition regarding a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period on the part of the insured, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid his liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches is/are so "fundamental" as found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
This is having regard to the "rule of main purpose" or "main purpose rule" i.e., even if there is a proof of the driver of a motor vehicle not being duly licenced at the time of the accident, the said fact must be a cause for the accident.
In other words, the breach was so fundamental as to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The doctrine of fundamental breach has been incorporated in Section 149 of the Act by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in order to give effect to the main purpose rule.
Thus, the exclusion clause or the defence of an insurer so as to avoid liability has been read down to the extent to which it is inconsistent to the main purpose of the contract.
Thus,
there has to be a finding of fact, as to, whether, the owner or the insured had taken reasonable care.
Hence, the Tribunal will have to decide the dispute, as to, whether, the insurer has proved its defence.
